findings.title: The site is missing 3 standard security headers
findings.detail: These headers stop other sites framing the page, sniffing its files as another type, and leaking full URLs to third parties. Missing: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options or a CSP frame-ancestors rule, Referrer-Policy.
findings.fix: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN (or a CSP frame-ancestors rule) and Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin from the web server or CDN.

evidence.note: missing: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options or a CSP frame-ancestors rule, Referrer-Policy

findings.title: 2 of 2 images have no width and height
findings.detail: Without width and height attributes the browser cannot reserve space for an image, so the text moves when it loads. That is the main cause of a poor layout-shift (CLS) score.
findings.fix: Add width and height attributes matching each image's real size, and keep max-width: 100% in the CSS so it still scales.

evidence.note: first image without width and height

findings.title: No organisation schema tells AI systems who runs this site
findings.detail: Organization or LocalBusiness markup gives AI systems a reliable source for the brand name, logo, location and profiles.

findings.title: The page does not answer questions in a form AI systems can lift
findings.detail: AI answers are built from passages that directly answer a question. Question headings with a short answer underneath are the easiest to cite.

evidence.note: no question headings and no FAQPage schema

findings.title: The site has no llms.txt file
findings.detail: llms.txt is an emerging convention that gives AI agents a short guide to the site. Google Search ignores it, so this is a small bonus, not a requirement.
findings.fix: Add a /llms.txt with a one-paragraph summary of the business and links to its most important pages.

findings.title: Nothing on the page says when it was written or last updated
findings.detail: AI answer engines and Google favour content that shows it is current. A machine-readable date (a Last-Modified header, a <time datetime> element, or datePublished/dateModified in the schema) is how they tell.
findings.fix: Add dateModified (and datePublished) to the page's JSON-LD, or wrap the "last updated" date in <time datetime="2026-01-31">.

evidence.note: no Last-Modified header, <time datetime>, article date meta tag or schema date found

findings.title: Nothing on the homepage says who is behind the business
findings.detail: Visitors, Google and AI systems look for an About page or a team to decide whether a business is real and who stands behind it. Google's quality guidelines call this trust.
findings.fix: Add an About page with who runs the business, how long it has operated and where, and link to it from the header or footer.

evidence.note: 19 links found, none to an about, team or company-story page

findings.title: There is no link to a privacy policy
findings.detail: A privacy policy is expected by visitors, by Google for sites that collect any data, and by Australian law for most businesses. Its absence is a trust signal against the site.
findings.fix: Publish a privacy policy and link to it from the footer of every page.

findings.title: The copy is hard to read
findings.detail: The reading ease score is 38. Most customers read at around a school-year-nine level, and scores below 50 mean long sentences and long words that lose them. Plain English converts better.
findings.fix: Shorten sentences to about 15 words, replace long words with short ones, and write the way you would explain it to a customer in person.

evidence.note: reading ease 38 over 863 words of paragraph text (50 or more is easy to read)
